root_cause_label: Wrong disk format + no state validation — the agent creates /app/isos/xp.img as qcow2 (not raw), launches QEMU without enforcing correct boot/install contract, never automates or verifies tb-admin creation, and declares completion based solely on service liveness (ports + CPU) without confirming XP reached the login screen.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent declares success from port and process liveness without verifying that Windows XP finished installing and reached the login screen with tb-admin, while also violating the task contract by creating the disk as qcow2 instead of raw.
t_commit_evidence: Step 4: The qcow2 disk is created and subsequently passed to QEMU at step 7 with `format=qcow2`; the wrong disk format is locked in from this point and the agent never pivots to correct it. The VM runs exclusively in this misconfigured state for the remainder of the trajectory.
t_surface_evidence: Setup verification: ... Windows XP installation in progress (99.9% CPU usage)
trigger_explanation: At step 4, the agent acts on the false premise that a qcow2 container is an acceptable disk format for this task. It never verifies the benchmark's artifact requirements and proceeds as if any QEMU-compatible image format suffices. This same false premise extends to treating QEMU process liveness (99.9% CPU) as a proxy for a completed Windows XP installation.
